drug_identity.off_label_note: Used extra-label for detecting corneal and conjunctival cell damage and evaluating tear film deficiencies.

cyp_profile.pathway_evidence: Topical diagnostic agent. Flushed from the eye after application; systemic absorption is minimal.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Stains both the nuclei and cell walls of dead or degenerated epithelial cells.

organ_burden_logic.note: Topical ophthalmic administration. Systemic organ burden is negligible. The primary concern is local toxicity to the cornea.

timing_profile.evidence: Acts locally and immediately stains damaged cells upon application.

_ddi_note: Ophthalmic preparations should not be mixed directly with any other ophthalmic medications. Rose bengal is virucidal and may confound diagnostic tests for viral keratitis; culture first.

dosage_list.context: Detection of corneal and conjunctival cell damage (extra-label)
dosage_list.duration_note: Wet the surface of the strip with 1-2 drops of normal saline, or instill 1 drop of 1% solution. Flush eye(s) thoroughly after exposure.

dosage_list.context: Detection of corneal and conjunctival cell damage (extra-label)
dosage_list.duration_note: Wet the surface of the strip with 1-2 drops of normal saline, or instill 1 drop of 1% solution. Flush eye(s) thoroughly after exposure.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Vital dye that stains both the nuclei and cell walls of dead or degenerated epithelial cells of the cornea and conjunctiva. Uptake is decreased in cells covered appropriately by mucin.

species_notes.dog: Has been demonstrated to be an effective adjunctive diagnostic test for evaluation of quantitative tear film deficiencies in dogs.

dog.evidence: Very toxic to the cornea; treated eye(s) should be thoroughly irrigated after exposure. Virucidal property may confound viral cultures.

cat.evidence: Very toxic to the cornea; treated eye(s) should be thoroughly irrigated after exposure. Virucidal property may confound viral cultures.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store in the refrigerator or at controlled room temperature (below 30°C) away from moisture and sunlight. Do not freeze.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Vital dye that demonstrates corneal/conjunctival epithelial cell damage and mucin deficiency. Very toxic to cornea; irrigate eye(s) well after use. Stings upon application.
section_1_2_10.indications: Detect epithelial cell damage prior to full-thickness epithelial cell loss (ulceration), evaluate qualitative (mucin) and quantitative tear deficiency syndromes.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Rose bengal strips should not be used by pet owners at home. Applied by a veterinarian.
